title: Reading for Comprehension
summary: Reading strategies, question types (literal, inferential, evaluative), quoting and answering in your own words, and using mark allocation, practised on an original passage.

items: **Skim** the passage for the general idea: title, first and last paragraphs, headings.
**Read** the questions so you know what to look for.
**Read closely**, marking key words and the writer's opinions.
**Scan** for specific details when answering each question.

rows: 'Why do you think…', 'What does this suggest…'
Response to the writer's style and effect

notes.text: Copy the exact words from the text inside quotation marks. Do not change spelling or add words.
Rephrase the idea; copying the text earns no marks.

notes.title: Practice passage: The Last Bookshop on Long Street (written for FreeSheet)
notes.text:
[1] When Mr Abrahams opened his bookshop in 1987, there were six others on the same street. Today his is the only one left. The shelves still sag under second-hand paperbacks, and the shop still smells of dust and coffee, but the customers are fewer and greyer.

[2] 'People tell me books are dying,' he says, smiling. 'They have been dying for as long as I have been selling them.' He points to a group of teenagers in the corner, sitting on the floor with a stack of comics. 'Those three come every Saturday. They hardly buy anything, but they read for hours. That is not a dying habit.'

[3] Still, the numbers worry him. Rent has tripled in ten years, and online stores sell new books for less than he pays for them. To survive, he has started a reading club and a book-swap table, and he hosts poetry evenings on the first Friday of every month. 'A bookshop cannot just sell books any more,' he says. 'It has to be a place people want to be.'

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Let the mark allocation guide you: 2 marks usually needs two points, or one point with an explanation. For a true/false question with a reason, the mark is given only if the reason (often a quotation) is correct.

questions.prompt: How many other bookshops were on the street when Mr Abrahams opened his shop?
In which year did the bookshop open?
'Why do you think Mr Abrahams smiles when he says books are dying?' This is a(n)…
What does 'the customers are fewer and greyer' suggest?
options: There are fewer customers and most are older

questions.prompt: According to paragraph 3, the rent has doubled in ten years.
Quote FOUR consecutive words from paragraph 3 that show the shop must offer more than books.
Match each question level to its description.
List THREE things Mr Abrahams has done to keep his shop open.
questions.memo:
✓ Started a reading club (1)
✓ Set up a book-swap table (1)
✓ Hosts monthly poetry evenings (1)

questions.prompt: Explain why the teenagers in paragraph 2 support Mr Abrahams's view.
questions.memo:
✓ They read for hours every Saturday (1)
✓ showing that young people still enjoy reading, so books are not 'dying' (1)

questions.prompt: Do you agree that 'a bookshop cannot just sell books any more'? Give reasons.
questions.memo:
✓ Clear stance (1)
✓✓ Two well-reasoned points, e.g. online competition is cheaper; people want experiences and community (2)
